note: Pre-registered 2026-11-05 BEFORE any run, to check whether the constraint fixes generalise beyond the three corrected pairs. Different businesses, wording and limits from reasoning-pairs.json. Each case is graded by checkAnswer() (mention check only) plus the rubric, read by a person. Not tuned after seeing answers.

cases.question: Should we redesign our onboarding flow? Sign-ups drop off at step two.

context.product_description: Booking app for independent physiotherapy clinics

constraints.text: Our only designer is on leave until January

cases.rubric: Proposes something doable now without design work (copy change, removing a field, calling drop-offs) and puts the redesign at January or later, saying why. Does not recommend starting the redesign now.

cases.question: An agency offers a 12-month SEO contract at a discount if we sign this week. Should we?

constraints.text: Cash covers about ten weeks of costs

cases.rubric: Treats the ten weeks of cash as the deciding risk; does not recommend a 12-month commitment that outlasts it; offers a short, stoppable alternative. No invented SEO benchmarks or payback figures.

cases.question: Walkers keep leaving our app. Should we lower our 20% fee to keep them?

context.product_description: Marketplace app matching dog walkers with owners

cases.rubric: Compares the fee explicitly with walkers taking regular clients directly for zero fee; asks what the app gives a walker once they know the owner. A lower rate alone is not presented as the fix.

cases.question: What conversion rate should I expect on my candle shop's website?

context.product_description: Scented candles sold through our own website

cases.rubric: Does not state a typical or industry conversion rate or range; says it has no supported figure, and explains how to measure their own baseline. Any figure given is explicitly marked as not supported by their data.

cases.question: A bank offered us a loan to buy a second delivery van. Should we take it?

context.product_description: Same-day courier service for local shops

constraints.text: We would rather not take on debt this year

cases.rubric: Treats 'rather not take on debt' as a preference that can be weighed, not a hard ban: may recommend the loan if the case is strong, says it is trading off their preference, and gives the no-debt option too.

round2.note: Pre-registered 2026-11-07 BEFORE any run, for the numeric-provenance retest. Graded by traceNumbers() (no unsupported figure) plus the rubric read by a person.

cases.question: What price should I charge for a new premium tier?

context.product_description: Online course platform for amateur photographers

cases.rubric: Uses only the supplied £12 (or a shown calculation from it); does not quote 'typical' premium multipliers or market prices; proposes how to find their own answer (test with a segment, ask current members). Any illustrative figure is labelled 'Illustration, not a benchmark'.

cases.question: Our payment provider charges us 3.4% per transaction. Is that normal?
cases.rubric: Does not assert what is 'normal' or 'typical' without a source; says it has no supported benchmark; can compute what 3.4% costs them if they give volume; suggests getting quotes or checking the provider's published pricing. The 3.4% itself is supplied.
